minutes.headline: Board reappointed election officers, approved the NewGen solar PILOT, and heard the school building enrollment update.
minutes.summary: The Select Board appointed election officers for the year, including the incumbent warden over a challenger. It approved the NewGen solar PILOT agreement and a change of manager for Mickey Shays. A long school building project update focused on whether enrollment projections are too tight before the state certification deadline. The board decided not to intervene in the Unitil rate case and went into executive session on the town manager's contract.

what_happened.line: The Select Board approved the NewGen solar PILOT agreement as written, by unanimous vote.
The board appointed election officers for the year, including the incumbent warden in a contested appointment; each appointment passed.
A long school building project update centered on whether enrollment projections are too tight before the state certification deadline.
The board decided not to file as an intervener in the Unitil rate case; members may attend the September 23 hearing and possibly send a letter later.
The board approved a change of manager for Mickey Shays and the Lakeview Driving Range base license, both unanimously, then entered executive session.

why_it_matters: The solar PILOT sets what a large solar site pays in personal property taxes for 20 years, so it shapes a stream of town revenue and what the assessor says about site valuation.

The school building project is still before the state's certification step, and the enrollment projections used there help set the size and cost of a project residents may later be asked to fund at Town Meeting and the ballot.
watch_next: Next week's agenda holds time for a school building discussion alongside the policies work session.
Town counsel's request to the assessor for written clarification on solar site valuation; the September 23 Unitil hearing.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most appointments, the PILOT, the Mickey Shea's manager change, the Lakeview license and the Unitil decision, but they disagree on who was present, the vote counts, and several decisions. The main thing to know is that the official minutes list Ms. Bertram as absent and Mr. Alonzo as present, while our minutes name Bertram as a member and never mention Alonzo. The official minutes also say several appointees (Edward Harriman, Darleen Steele, L. Grace Harriman) were not present, and they record 4-0-1 or 3-0-1 votes for those appointments.
